newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cocoa producers urge respect for world pact.
newsitem.headline: Cocoa producers urge respect for world pact.

text.p: The Codex committee for chocolate and cocoa products should respect the 1993 world cocoa agreement and promote consumption, a Brussels-based lobby group for leading world producers said.

The Codex committee, administered by the World Health Organisation and the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation, is due to finish a three-day meeting in Thoune, Switzerland on Wednesday on a revision of the Codex Alimentarius - which sets a wide range of food standards.

In a statement, the cocoa producing countries secretariat urged the committee "to reject any revisions...which are in clear violation of the signed International Cocoa Agreement and in detriment to the consumer."
One proposed revision would allow up to five percent non-cocoa butter vegetable fats in chocolate products.
"The 5 percent clause for non-cocoa butter vegetable fats would have enormous consequences...," the cocoa producers said, estimating cocoa demand could fall from 80,000 to 200,000 tonnes.
Chocolate labels would also no longer have to include a reference to vegetable fats next to the name of the product.
Another revision would lower the percentage of cocoa solids in milk chocolate to 20 percent from 25 percent.

The 1993 cocoa agreement, signed by 38 importing and exporting countries, stated that all members should take "all practicable measures which may be necessary to encourage the expansion of cocoa consumption in their own countries."
The secretariat represents Brazil, Cameroon, Ecuador, Ghana, Ivory Coast and Venezuela.
